Note: I did not find the user's functional-design skills under ~/.claude/skills, so this audit uses the provisional rubric.

sites.construct: synchronized + AtomicBoolean CAS + try/catch per step + AllowUnsafe inbox.unsafe.close + Thread.currentThread().interrupt()
sites.what: This is the one synchronous release. The current code gives these guarantees. G1: canvas.close() runs first. It takes the backend monitor, so it waits for a draw in progress, and no frame is drawn after the restore (Paint.scala:51, :166-171). G2: the input loop is stopped, then the inbox is closed. This wakes an input put that waits for room (backpressure), and the runner ends at its next take (Runner.scala:211-213). G3: the release joins the input thread, bounded at 2*poll+50 ms (100 ms by default). It records 'input-hung' and goes on, so a native poll that hangs cannot block the exit. G4: then leave runs. It sends DisableBracketedPaste (when paste is on), then Show (cursor), then LeaveAlternateScreen. Then it turns raw mode off, flushes, stops the output capture, finishes the sink (logs and captured output go to the real stderr only after the restore), removes the shutdown hook (not when it runs inside the hook), prints the R3 warning and the first error, and calls restored() (the latch of TuiApp). G5: every step runs even if an earlier step failed. G6: the release is idempotent, and a second caller (the hook thread or the release of the fiber) WAITS on the monitor until the first caller is done. So the JVM cannot halt in the middle of a restore. G7: an interrupt does not cut the release short. The flag is set again at the end. G8: the release depends on no Kyo scheduler. On SIGTERM, kill -INT, SIGHUP or System.exit, the tui4s-restore hook runs it on a plain JVM thread. TuiApp's tui4s-stop hook also interrupts the fiber and waits at most 2 s for restored. G9: on a quit or a UI failure, Scope.run (the user's Scope.ensure) closes INSIDE the use of the bracket, so it runs before the restore (Tui.scala:150-152). Lock order: the Session monitor, then the backend monitor. A flush holds only the backend monitor, so there is no deadlock. Note on Ctrl-C: in raw mode Ctrl-C is a key, not SIGINT. ctrlCQuits makes it a quit.
sites.why: The JVM shutdown hook has no fiber. It must run the restore synchronously on its own thread, and it must not depend on a Kyo scheduler that may be busy.
sites.replacement:
Keep this as one synchronous function. Do NOT move it into Scope finalizers: those run on Async, they need the scheduler during shutdown, and Fiber.init AWAITS its fibers (kyo Fiber.scala:139-145). Clean up the inside of the function only.

private[tui4s] object Release:
  final case class Outcome(first: Maybe[Throwable], interrupted: Boolean)
  def all(steps: (() => Unit)*): Outcome =
    steps.foldLeft(Outcome(Absent, false)) { (o, step) =>
      try { step(); o }
      catch
        case e: VirtualMachineError  => throw e
        case _: InterruptedException => o.copy(interrupted = true)
        case e: Throwable            => if o.first.isEmpty then o.copy(first = Present(e)) else o
    }

def close()(using AllowUnsafe, Frame): Unit = synchronized {
  if !closed then                     // a plain field under the monitor; the CAS goes
    closed = true
    val out = Release.all(
      () => canvas.close(),                          // G1
      () => Session.closeInbox(inbox),               // G2 (also stops the input loop)
      () => thread.foreach(joinOrHang),              // G3
      () => control.leave(opts, entered))            // G4
    if out.interrupted then Thread.currentThread().interrupt() // G7
}

G5 and G6 are kept by Release.all and the monitor. G8 is kept because nothing here uses Async. G9 is kept if Tui.onTerminal keeps Scope.run inside the use of acquireReleaseWith.
sites.risk: terminal restore and concurrency. The step order G1 to G4 is load-bearing. Release.all makes Session use the policy 'catch all but VirtualMachineError', as TerminalIO.leave does. Today Session.safely catches only NonFatal, so a LinkageError in an early step would skip control.leave. The practical risk is low, because no early step makes a JNI call. The SessionTest order logs ('input-stopped', 'input-joined') must stay.

sites.construct: while loop + var left + try/catch InterruptedException + System.nanoTime + Thread.join
sites.what: Waits until a deadline for the input thread. When the wait is interrupted, it records the interrupt and waits again.
sites.why: Thread.join is the only way to wait for a platform thread. An interrupt must not cut the wait short (G3, G7).
sites.replacement:
@tailrec def join(t: Thread, deadline: Long, intr: Boolean): (Boolean, Boolean) =
  val left = deadline - System.nanoTime()
  if !t.isAlive || left <= 0 then (!t.isAlive, intr)
  else Result.catching[InterruptedException](t.join(java.time.Duration.ofNanos(left))) match
    case Result.Failure(_) => join(t, deadline, true)   // recursion outside the try, so it stays tailrec
    case _                 => (!t.isAlive, intr)
The interrupt flag goes into Release.Outcome. Then the `interrupted` field (Session.scala:64) goes too.
sites.risk: terminal restore: the bound of the join must stay. Without it, a hung native poll blocks the exit.

sites.construct: Sync.Unsafe.defer with a try/catch nested in a try/catch, var session: Session | Null, a defensive try around control.leave (:177-178), throw e
sites.what: Enters the terminal, makes the Canvas and the input thread, starts the thread, and registers the hook. A failure after the session exists calls s.close(). A failure before it exists calls control.leave(). The result is an Either.
sites.why: The acquire of the bracket must be ONE step, with no map after it, so that an interrupt cannot drop an open session (guarantee G10). The var lets the catch know how far the acquire went.
sites.replacement:
Keep the single Sync.Unsafe.defer (G10), and build the session in stages, with no var:
Sync.Unsafe.defer {
  control.enter(opts) match                         // Result[TuiError, (Backend, Entered)]; it undoes its own steps
    case Result.Success((backend, entered)) =>
      Result.catching[Throwable](Session(Canvas(backend), control, opts, inbox, entered, threadFor(input))) match
        case Result.Failure(e) => control.leave(opts, entered); Left(TuiError.TerminalIO(e))
        case Result.Success(s) =>
          Result.catching[Throwable] { s.thread.foreach(_.start()); control.opened(() => s.close()) }
            .fold(_ => Right(s))(e => { s.close(); Left(asTuiError(e)) })
    case Result.Failure(e) => Left(e)
}
leave never throws (all but VirtualMachineError are caught), so the try at :177-178 goes.
sites.risk: terminal restore: a failure between raw mode and the hook registration must still undo everything (G11). Keep this as one step for the bracket.

sites.construct: Thread subclass + while loops + var + volatile + mutable buffer + j.u.c. latch + catch Throwable
sites.what: A platform daemon thread. It calls poll(pollMillis), then reads every queued event (at most 512), maps the events to Msg values, and puts them as one batch, blocking while the inbox is full (backpressure). On a failure it keeps the error and puts Msg.Quit.
sites.why: Keep the THREAD. The native read() cannot be interrupted. A daemon thread whose poll hangs does not keep the JVM alive. Also, a JNI poll on a Kyo worker would count as load in SchedulerProbe, so `busy <= 1 && total <= 1` would fail and every settle would run until its max (100 ms per frame). The loop BODY does not need its mutable state.
sites.replacement:
override def run(): Unit =
  import AllowUnsafe.embrace.danger
  val forever = new Clock.Deadline.Unsafe(Absent, Clock.live.unsafe)
  def stopped = inbox.unsafe.closed()              // replaces `running`: the release closes the inbox (G2)
  @tailrec def batch(n: Int, seq: Long, acc: Chunk[Msg]): (Long, Chunk[Msg]) =
    if stopped || n >= 512 || (n > 0 && !port.poll(0)) then (seq, acc)
    else port.read().flatMap(EventMapping(_, seq)) match
      case Present(m) => batch(n + 1, seq + 1, acc.append(m))
      case Absent     => batch(n + 1, seq, acc)
  @tailrec def loop(seq: Long): Unit =
    if !stopped then
      if port.poll(pollMillis) then
        val (next, msgs) = batch(0, seq, Chunk.empty)
        if msgs.nonEmpty then discard(inbox.unsafe.putBatchFiber(msgs).block(forever)) // a closed inbox gives Closed
        loop(next)
      else loop(seq)
  try loop(1L)
  catch
    case _: InterruptedException => ()
    case e: VirtualMachineError  => throw e
    case e: Throwable            => failed.set(Present(e)); discard(inbox.unsafe.putFiber(Msg.Quit))
`failed` is an AtomicRef.Unsafe[Maybe[Throwable]], the same cell that Kyo's KyoAppInterrupts uses for a value written by another thread.
sites.risk: concurrency. Keep the backpressure, and keep the guarantee that closing the inbox releases a blocked put (the Fiber.Unsafe.block of Kyo parks with LockSupport and returns when the put fiber completes with Closed). Keep the poll-before-read rule. The catch must keep LinkageError as a failure of the input. SessionTest.scala:96 calls requestStop(): it must close the inbox instead.

sites.construct: var undo: List[() => Unit] + throw TuiError.NotATerminal / TerminalIO + try/catch around each step + catch Throwable with rethrow + the undo loop
sites.what: Steps of the acquire: (1) load the native library, (2) start the output capture and its R3 check, (3) check that stdin is a tty, (4) raw mode, (5) the mode commands. The undo of the modes is registered BEFORE the execute, because a command list that fails can be half done. A failure runs the undos in reverse order, then sink.finish(err), then throws again.
sites.why: Expected conditions (stdin is not a tty, raw mode is refused) travel as exceptions, and the undo stack is mutable.
sites.replacement:
type Undo = () => Unit
// each acquire gives the undo to keep (also on a half-done failure) and its result
type Acquire = () => (Maybe[Undo], Result[TuiError, Unit])
val acquires: List[Acquire] = List(load, capture(opts), ttyCheck, raw, modes(opts))
@tailrec def go(as: List[Acquire], undos: List[Undo]): Result[TuiError, Unit] = as match
  case Nil => Result.unit
  case a :: rest =>
    val (u, r) = a(); val us = u.toList ++ undos
    r match
      case Result.Success(_) => go(rest, us)
      case failed            => discard(Release.all(us*)); sink.finish(err); failed
The undo list is built by prepending, so it is already in reverse order. The JNI calls keep their own catch, which maps an error to a TuiError.
sites.risk: terminal restore (G11). The undo order must stay: leave the modes, raw mode off, stop the capture, then sink.finish. Keep the half-done rule for the command list. load stays first, so the three errors that come before any terminal change still come before the terminal changes.

sites.what: Builds the command lists for the alternate screen, Clear, Hide and bracketed paste, and their reverse.
sites.why: Convenience.
sites.replacement:
final case class Mode(on: Command, off: Maybe[Command])
def modes(o: TuiOptions): List[Mode] =
  List(Mode(Command.EnterAlternateScreen(), Present(Command.LeaveAlternateScreen())),
       Mode(Command.Clear(ClearType.All), Absent),
       Mode(Command.Hide(), Present(Command.Show()))) ++
  Option.when(o.paste)(Mode(Command.EnableBracketedPaste(), Present(Command.DisableBracketedPaste())))
def enterCommands(o: TuiOptions) = modes(o).map(_.on)
def leaveCommands(o: TuiOptions) = modes(o).reverse.flatMap(_.off.toList)  // paste off, Show, LeaveAlternateScreen: the same order as today

sites.construct: Runtime.addShutdownHook / removeShutdownHook, catch IllegalStateException, a probe Thread for shuttingDown (an exception used as control flow)
sites.what: Registers and removes the restore hook. Finds out whether the JVM is shutting down by adding and removing a dummy hook.
sites.why: The JDK has no public query for a shutdown in progress. A flag that one of our own hooks sets would race: the JVM starts the hooks concurrently, in no fixed order. The probe is exact, because the registry of hooks closes when the shutdown starts.
sites.replacement: Keep the code as it is. Move it into its own small file (JvmHooks.scala) as part of the boundary module. The four Runtime.getRuntime.nn calls stay (explicit nulls at the Java boundary).
sites.risk: terminal restore (G8). TuiApp uses shuttingDown to skip onExit and its prints.

smells.smell: A gap in the restore guarantee. The JVM restore hook is registered LAST, after raw mode, the alternate screen, the canvas and the start of the input thread. Under plain Tui.run (no tui4s-stop hook from TuiApp), a SIGTERM during enter leaves the shell in raw mode and in the alternate screen. Under TuiApp it is covered: hooks.add throws IllegalStateException, the catch calls s.close(), and the fiber's interrupt goes through the bracket.
smells.fix: Register the hook FIRST, before load and raw mode. Give it a release that undoes only the steps entered so far. With the immutable Entered value, or an AtomicRef.Unsafe[Entered] that grows as each step succeeds, the hook knows how far the acquire went.

smells.smell: Duplicated logic. Four hand-written copies of 'run every step, keep the first error', with DIFFERENT catch policies: Session.safely catches NonFatal and InterruptedException; enter's undo catches all but VirtualMachineError and drops the errors; leave catches all but VirtualMachineError and keeps the first; Session.open catches NonFatal and drops the errors. A LinkageError in an early step of Session.close would skip control.leave.
smells.fix: Use one Release.all(steps*): Outcome(first: Maybe[Throwable], interrupted: Boolean) with one policy (all but VirtualMachineError), and use it in all four places.

smells.smell: A god object. The settle loop, the scheduler probe policy, verify and repair, the application of content, the layout and focus repair (fixFocus, relayoutAll and layoutStep are pure and use only options.autoFocus), and the FrameStats are all in one class that has mutable fields.
smells.fix: Split it into Settler (settle, hop, probe), Repair (verify, repairAll, verifyRegion), a pure object FrameLayout (fixFocus, relayoutAll, layoutStep, with autoFocus as a parameter), and a thin Runner that only loops and holds the seams.

smells.smell: A god state. World mixes the UI state, the counters of each step (updates, repaired, settleTimeouts, which are reset by hand at each step), control flags (quit, full) and a queue of messages (backlog).
smells.fix: Thread the counters as a separate StepStats value (or as a Kyo Var[StepStats] that is run for each step), and keep the backlog in the Loop state of the runner. Then World holds only what is on the screen.

smells.smell: Duplicated classification of Msg. Two matches on Key, Paste and Resize, one to find `input` and one to find (seq, cause). The isCtrlC test is in handle and also in ending.
smells.fix: Add `def inputSeq: Maybe[Long]` to Msg. Then input = msg.inputSeq.isDefined, and cause = inputSeq.fold(Background)(_ => Input).

smells.smell: Stringly typed data. The steps of the session are the strings "input-started", "input-stopped", "input-joined" and "input-hung".
smells.fix: Use `enum SessionStep { InputStarted, InputStopped, InputJoined, InputHung }`. RecordingControl writes the kebab-case names to its log, so the test assertions do not change.

smells.smell: Exceptions are used for expected outcomes. NotATerminal and NativeAccessDenied are thrown, then caught and made into an Either.
smells.fix: Use `enter: Result[TuiError, (Backend, Entered)]`. Use throw only for errors that the JVM makes fatal.

smells.smell: Null sentinels: InputThread | Null, Throwable | Null (twice), CEvent | Null, Msg | Null.
smells.fix: Use Maybe[...]. Convert with Maybe(x) only on the Java line that returns the value.

smells.smell: The seams of the effect system are spread out. AllowUnsafe and Sync.Unsafe are used in five files, and there is no single boundary module.
smells.fix: Make one boundary package, tui4s.internal.term, with Session, TerminalIO, JvmHooks, Crossterm, InputThread and Release. Put the only AllowUnsafe / Sync.Unsafe.defer calls in Session.open and Session.close (and the hook thread). Runner then has none.

audits.sliceVerdict: This slice is not 'whiles everywhere'. Runner (749 lines) already has a Kyo shape: Loop, Kyo.foldLeft, Abort.run, Async.timeout and a pure World. Its problems are few and cheap to fix: four java.util.concurrent atomics, two impure reads outside an effect (nanoTime at Runner.scala:672, the scheduler probe at :503), two casts, and a Result wildcard that turns a Panic into a clean quit. The impure code is in the right files (Session, TerminalIO, Crossterm, InputThread), but it is written like Java: 9 volatile or var fields, null sentinels, a mutable undo stack, four copies of 'run every step, keep the first error' with different catch policies, and exceptions for expected errors such as NotATerminal. The restore logic is careful and correct (guarantees G1 to G11 are on the Session.close site). Keep it as one synchronous release that does not use the Kyo scheduler and that a JVM hook can call; do not move it into Scope finalizers. The single most valuable change is in Runner: replace last/remember/ticker/stopped with Sync.ensure(mount.interruptAll) around Fiber.use(repairTick). That deletes about 40 lines, six remember calls and two review-fix windows, and it does not touch the terminal restore. Next, add one Release combinator and an immutable Entered value from enter: that removes the four volatile fields of TerminalIO, makes the catch policy the same everywhere, and lets the restore hook be registered first, which closes the SIGTERM-during-enter gap under plain Tui.run.

audits.slice: Reactive tree: modules/core/src/main/scala/tui4s/internal/{Mount,Dispatch,Render,World,ComponentSpec,Props,EventMapping}.scala and modules/core/src/main/scala/tui4s/{Component,Hooks}.scala (main checkout, read-only). There was no functional-design or Scala skill under /root/.claude/skills in this container (only session-start-hook and the synced Anthropic skills), so this uses the provisional rubric.

sites.construct: java.util.Collections.synchronizedSet(newSetFromMap(WeakHashMap[Fiber, Boolean])), started.synchronized(...) iteration, an impure `track(f): Unit`, 3 CollectionConverters imports
sites.what: The live-fiber gauge. Every watcher, hook or onMount fiber and the repair tick are added to it. liveFibers counts the fibers that are not done (a test gauge), and interruptAll interrupts all of them at stop (the R2-1 window: a watcher that a step started but did not remember yet).
sites.why: The gauge must not keep dead fibers alive (so the set is weak). interruptAll is the safety net for the fibers that a step started inside a settle.
sites.risk: Concurrency and the end of the run. Strong references with removal on completion are exact, and they also close a latent hole: a hook or onMount fiber parked on Async.never that the World dropped (the R2-1 window) is reachable only from the weak set. GC could collect it before interruptAll, and then its Scope finalizers never run (PLAUSIBLE, not reproduced). The Runner constructor (outside the slice) must build Mount inside an effect. WatcherTest, ComponentTest and HooksTest gauge asserts must stay green.

sites.construct: java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap[Loc, java.lang.Long] shared between the watcher fibers and the runner; unarmedRegions mutates the map (remove) inside a flatMap, outside any effect
sites.what: The armkey set (D-16): the regions whose watcher has not reached its arm step. watch puts the entry, the watcher's step 0 removes it before it posts Msg.Armed, and Runner.verify reads it on Input steps.
sites.why: The verify pass must re-read the regions that can still miss a write (the lost wakeup of Signal in Kyo RC7, TODO #8).
sites.risk: Concurrency semantics of D-16. The World set is a superset of the map: an entry leaves when the runner absorbs Armed, after the watcher removed it. So verify can only re-read more often, never less. Every Armed message is handled (Runner.scala:238 and :415). SeamTest (armkey) must stay green. Runner is touched (2 lines).

sites.construct: fe0.asInstanceOf[Foreach[Any, UI]]
sites.what: Opens the existential item type of a kyo-ui Foreach so that key, render and signal can be applied.
sites.why: The comment says erasure forces it (kyo-ui's applyTyped is private). A Scala 3 type-variable pattern opens the existential without a cast.
sites.replacement:
case fe: Foreach[a, ?] =>   // a is bound: fe.signal: Signal[Chunk[a]], fe.render: (Int, a) => UI
  ... reconcile(fe, Vector.empty, values.toVector) ...

// Source.Many(fe: Foreach[?, ?]); Runner.apply opens it with the same pattern
sites.risk: None at run time. One cast stays in Runner.scala:379 (c.value.asInstanceOf[Chunk[Any]]) until Msg.Content carries a typed value (see the smells).

sites.construct: 2 casts: ref.asInstanceOf[SignalRef[c.State]] and state.asInstanceOf[SignalRef[Any]]
sites.what: Stores and loads the state of a Component across instances (a parent that renders again builds a new instance with the same key).
sites.why: Component#State is a path-dependent type member. For a new instance c, nothing proves c.State = old.State, so a cast is unavoidable without a type witness. The real hole: stateKey is a user string that can be overridden, and it decides the cast. Two classes with one key and different State types give a ClassCastException in user code. The Scaladoc of stateKey documents this.
sites.replacement: Keep one cast in one helper: private def stateOf(c: Component)(r: SignalRef[Any]): SignalRef[c.State] = r.asInstanceOf. Key comps by (path, c.getClass, stateKey) so that the key cannot pair two classes (the hole then remains only for one generic class with different type arguments). A full fix needs `protected given Tag[State]` on Component (a public API change).
sites.risk: Public API: the documented sharing of state across classes with one key goes away if the class joins the key.

sites.construct: Fiber.initUnscoped plus `.map(f => Sync.defer { track(f); f })`, repeated 3 times; Abort.run[Throwable](...).unit and `case _ => post(UI.empty)` drop failures silently
sites.what: Starts the watcher, the hook-component body and the onMount fiber. Each is owned by RegionState.watcher, interrupted at unmount, and interrupted at stop by interruptAll.
sites.why: Unscoped on purpose: a run-owned Scope waits for a CPU-bound fiber at close (Fiber.init's release awaits the fiber; spike S2). Keep initUnscoped. The duplication and the silent failures are what to fix.
sites.risk: Concurrency: low. The interrupt order stays the same. Log must go to the file sink (AGENTS: no stdout while the UI runs). Dispatch.safe already uses Log.error.

sites.construct: reclaim.removed(path)
sites.what: Removes the component's own path from the reclaim map before it walks the content.
sites.why: Defensive. The nested walk only looks up paths under path :+ "~", so it can never look up `path`, and the call has no effect.
sites.replacement: walk(content, path :+ "~", ..., reclaim)
sites.risk: None.

sites.construct: A global mutable registry: Collections.synchronizedMap(WeakHashMap[Signal[?], ComponentSpec]). node() writes it from pure-typed public code (Component.ui: Reactive[UI], Hooks.component: UI), and lookup reads it with no effect
sites.what: Marks a kyo-ui Reactive as a component node by the identity of its signal (K3).
sites.why: A true boundary: the kyo-ui AST is sealed, and kyo.Signal is a `sealed abstract class` (Signal.scala:44 in RC7). tui4s cannot subclass Signal or add a node type, so a registry keyed by identity is the only side channel. Each entry is written once for a fresh signal before the UI value can be seen, so a lookup is deterministic (it acts like the read of an immutable field). Weak keys tie the entry to the UI value. No value holds its key, so nothing leaks.
sites.replacement: Keep it in this file as the one seam, with this reason in its Scaladoc. Do not make node() effectful: that changes the public return types (Hooks.component: UI, the implicit conversion componentToChild).
sites.risk: Public API if anyone changes it. Global state (the second global after the output capture).

sites.why: Redundant. The package-level inline discard (internal/package.scala:7) is in scope and this copy shadows it.

sites.risk: None.

sites.construct: import AllowUnsafe.embrace.danger; Signal.SignalRef.Unsafe.init[State](initial).safe inside the lazy fallback
sites.what: The UI that a foreign kyo-ui runner (DOM, server push) sees: one state per node value, built the first time it is needed.
sites.why: A foreign-runner boundary. The fallback must be a plain UI inside Signal.currentWith, and it is memoized by `lazy val fb` in ComponentSpec.node. A Sync allocation per read would give a new state on each read. The allocation is one-shot and local.
sites.replacement: Move the unsafe allocation into ComponentSpec (the one seam): ComponentSpec.node(Instance(this), ComponentSpec.ownState(initial)(view)) with `def ownState[A: CanEqual](init: A)(view: SignalRef[A] => UI): UI = { import AllowUnsafe.embrace.danger; view(Signal.SignalRef.Unsafe.init(init).safe) }`. Then Component.scala has no AllowUnsafe.
sites.risk: None (internal to ui).

audits.sliceVerdict: This slice is not "whiles everywhere". The 9 files have no while or do loop, no var, no return, no try/catch/throw and no Thread. The tree is already one immutable World threaded through Kyo Loop, Kyo.foldLeft and plain recursion, and Props is fully pure. The impurity is in a few places: two Java concurrent collections in Mount (the weak fiber gauge and the armkey map, which is mutated with no effect in unarmedRegions), the impure callback in Tui4sTrack, null as absence in EventMapping, and a test-only renderer in main. Two sites are justified boundaries: the global component registry (Signal and the kyo-ui AST are sealed) and the AllowUnsafe fallback in Component.ui. The real reason it reads badly is the data model: RegionState, Content and Msg carry Any payloads, fields that are valid only for some sources, duplicated state and string keys, and those cause the casts and the copy-paste in Dispatch. On top of that, World is a 17-field god object, and 89 change-log comment lines bury the logic. The one purity change with the most value, for small cost: move the unarmed map into World and replace the weak set with a Kyo AtomicRef gauge (removal on completion). Mount then holds no shared mutable state, and that also closes a latent GC hole for fibers parked on Async.never. The follow-up with the most design value is a sealed per-source Region ADT with typed Msg.Content (cost L).

sites.construct: side effects outside an effect: 25 direct canvas.put/text/clear/fillBg calls that return Unit, inside an object that looks pure
sites.what: Walks the immutable Laid and writes cells straight into the mutable jatatui back Buffer while it decides what to draw. Runner.scala:693 calls it inside one big Sync.defer. Render.scala:23 calls it with no effect at all.
sites.why: Simplest way to paint. Deciding what to draw and writing the cells are mixed together.
sites.replacement:
Make the painter pure and do one final write. All of Paint becomes a function from immutable input to immutable output, threading an accumulator the same way Layout threads `acc: Laid`:
```scala
enum Op:
  case Clear(r: Rect, bg: Option[JColor])
  case Fill(r: Rect, bg: JColor)                          // clipped in plan
  case Run(x: Int, y: Int, n: Int, sym: String, st: JStyle) // border side, field fill; clipped
  case Glyph(x: Int, y: Int, sym: String, st: JStyle)
  case Text(x: Int, y: Int, s: String, st: JStyle, clip: Rect)
final case class FramePlan(ops: Chunk[Op], dirty: Vector[Rect], subtrees: Int)

object Paint:
  def plan(laid: Laid, env: Scene, damage: Vector[Damage]): FramePlan =
    val clears = damage.collect { case c: Damage.Clear => c }.distinct
    val top    = ...                                   // as today
    val ops0   = Chunk.from(clears.map(c => Op.Clear(c.rect, c.bg)))
    val ops    = top.foldLeft(ops0)((acc, p) => node(laid, env, p, clipOf(laid, p), acc))
    FramePlan(ops, clears.map(_.rect) ++ top.flatMap(laid.nodes.get(_).map(_.rect)), top.size)
  private def node(laid: Laid, env: Scene, p: Loc, clip: Rect, acc: Chunk[Op]): Chunk[Op] = ... acc.append(op) ...

// Runner.frame:
canvas.draw(Paint.plan(w1.laid, w1.env, damage))   // FrameOut(cells, sent, subtrees) < (Sync & Abort[TuiError])
```
Use `Chunk.append`, which is O(1). Do not use `++`: Kyo `Chunk.concat` copies both arrays, so it would cost O(n·depth). A border becomes 4 Run ops and 4 Glyph ops, not one op per cell, so the op count is O(nodes). scrollStart, textValue, checkedValue and pickerValue are already pure and stay as they are.
sites.risk: perf: one small Op allocation per text line, border side or decoration, never per cell. Check it with the existing FrameStats and LeakProbe. Test API: SessionTest.scala:224-239 calls canvas.put and canvas.flush directly, so it must change. No public API change, because tui4s.internal is sealed.

sites.construct: try/catch + throw (an exception used for control flow)
sites.what: Canvas.terminalIO catches an IOException from the backend and throws TuiError.TerminalIO. Inside Runner's Sync.defer this becomes a Panic, and Tui.scala:126 maps `Result.Panic(e: TuiError)` back to a failure.
sites.why: Canvas methods are plain Unit methods with no effect type, so a throw was the only way to report a failure.
sites.risk: terminal restore: an Abort failure must still run the Session release bracket. It does, because the release is a Scope/ensure finalizer. concurrency: the monitor stays as it is. The effect type widens through Runner.

sites.construct: var (a hidden counter) + takeWrites() (a side channel)
sites.what: Counts the cells written since the last call. Runner.scala:695 reads and resets it after each flush, to report the 'cells repainted' frame stat.
sites.why: Canvas methods return Unit, so the count has no other way out.
sites.replacement: The write kernel returns its count: `write(op): Int` (Clear and Fill give r.w*r.h after the clip, Text gives setStringn's end.x - sx). Canvas.draw returns `FrameOut(cells, sent, subtrees)`. Delete `writes` and takeWrites. This is part of the draw seam above.
sites.risk: none beyond the frame-stats tests

sites.construct: while busy-wait on System.nanoTime, inside backend.synchronized, on the runner fiber
sites.what: Test seam Knobs.flushSeam. When it is set, the draw goes one row at a time and the thread spins between rows, so HeadlessTest.scala:99 can show that a reader never sees a torn frame.
sites.why: It makes the race window wide in a test. In a real run the knob is zero.
sites.replacement: Move the knob out of the production Canvas. Headless wraps its TestBackend in a test-only decorator whose `draw` splits the list by row and calls `LockSupport.parkNanos(seam)` between the rows. Canvas still calls draw under its monitor, so the test keeps its meaning. Canvas.resize matches `case tb: TestBackend` (Paint.scala:73), so the decorator must expose resize, or the match must see through it. Smallest fallback: keep the knob and replace the spin with `LockSupport.parkNanos(flushSeamNanos)`, which burns no CPU and still holds the monitor.
sites.risk: concurrency: HeadlessTest torn-frame test. perf: none in a real run.

sites.construct: var closed + synchronized on a foreign object (the Backend)
sites.what: close() is called from the JVM shutdown hook thread through Session.close. It waits for a draw in progress and then blocks every later draw. Headless reads under the same monitor, so it never sees a torn frame.
sites.why: A true cross-thread boundary. The shutdown hook runs outside the Kyo scheduler, and only a blocking JVM monitor can wait for the draw to end.
sites.replacement: Keep the monitor, but let Canvas own it: `private val lock = new Object`, `def close()(using AllowUnsafe): Unit = lock.synchronized { closed = true }`, and `def read[A](f: Backend => A)(using Frame): A < Sync = Sync.defer(lock.synchronized(f(backend)))`. Headless then calls `canvas.read(Screen.of)` and no longer locks the backend itself. The lock protocol then lives in one file.
sites.risk: concurrency and terminal restore: the shutdown hook must still wait for the last frame. Keep the existing Session and Headless tests.

sites.construct: private var back/front (mutable jatatui Buffers swapped on resize); Canvas.apply calls backend.size() with no effect
sites.what: The kept back buffer and the copy of the terminal (front). Resize replaces them. The constructor makes a foreign call. Its callers wrap it in Sync.defer (Headless.scala:321, tests), but Session.scala:154 and Render.scala:19 call it inside plain code.
sites.why: jatatui Buffer and Cell are mutable and not thread-safe. Runner and Session share one Canvas instance, so the buffers are swapped inside it instead of building a new Canvas.
sites.replacement: Keep the vars. Move Canvas from Paint.scala into its own boundary file, Canvas.scala. Its whole surface becomes: `init(backend): Canvas < Sync`, `draw(plan)`, `resize(size)` (both `< (Sync & Abort[TuiError])`), `size: Size < Sync`, `read(f)`, and `close()(using AllowUnsafe)`. Only the private kernel touches Buffer.
sites.risk: concurrency: only the runner fiber may touch back and front. Keep that comment in the code.

sites.construct: per-cell nested Range loops that mutate jatatui Cells
sites.what: Reset or fill every cell of a damaged rect, and write glyphs and strings into the back buffer.
sites.why: This is the real per-frame hot path. It touches O(damaged cells) foreign mutable Cells.
sites.replacement: Keep it as the private `write(op): Int` kernel of Canvas.draw, and say there that it is the hot path. sites.construct: a side effect hidden in a for/yield over iterators (`front.content(front.indexOf(x, y)) = copy.copy()`), plus a write to jatatui's public Cell[] field
sites.what: Diffs back against front inside the dirty rects, updates front, and collects BufferUpdates. When dirty rects overlap, a cell is sent only once, and only because the front write happens lazily before the next compare.
sites.why: The per-cell diff is a true hot loop. It was written in an iterator style that looks pure but is not.
sites.replacement:
Keep it as a kernel, but make the effect explicit, for example:
```scala
private def diff(dirty: Vector[Rect]): Vector[BufferUpdate] =
  val out = Vector.newBuilder[BufferUpdate]
  for r <- dirty; c = r.intersect(screen); y <- c.y until c.bottom; x <- c.x until c.right do
    val b = back.cellAt(x, y)
    if b != front.cellAt(x, y) then
      val copy = b.copy()
      front.content(front.indexOf(x, y)) = copy.copy()
      out += BufferUpdate(x, y, copy)
  out.result()
```
Keep the double copy. back's cells are mutated again by reset and setBg, and the backend may keep the instance it gets.
sites.risk: perf: hot loop. Correctness: overlapping rects still give one update per cell, because the front write happens before the next visit.

smells.where: Layout.scala:575-582 vs 341-348 (measuredKids table branch vs rowsOf)
smells.smell: Duplicated logic that has drifted. This is a PLAUSIBLE real bug. measuredKids takes all tbody children (no Tr filter) and throws away `itemsOf(tb, ...).regions`. So a Reactive or Foreach directly inside a tbody is never put in regionOwner. When it changes, Runner.scala:640 finds no owner and drops the update, so a `table(tbody(foreach(sig)(tr(...))))` would stay stale until a full layout. There is no tbody test.
smells.fix: Use one rowsOf for both paths. It returns typed rows plus the regions of the table and of each tbody, and measuredKids and tableSize both use it. Add a RelayoutTest with a foreach inside a tbody.

smells.smell: layoutChildren and relayout repeat the same block: measuredKids, then content box, then tableCols, then arrange, then Ctx, then the regionOwner update.
smells.fix: Extract `arrangeKids(node, env, root): Arranged(kids, regions, rects, ctx, cols)` and a `register(laid, node, kids, regions)` step. Both functions then call them.

smells.where: Layout.scala:73-79 (Laid.without), called per changed kid at 785 and 808
smells.smell: A per-frame perf trap on a hot path. Each removal filters the whole nodes Map, so the cost is O(N) per changed kid. A Foreach of 1000 rows that changes costs O(N·k) every frame.
smells.fix: It can stay pure. Walk the subtree through node.kids: `def sub(p: Loc): Iterator[Loc] = Iterator(p) ++ nodes.get(p).iterator.flatMap(_.kids.iterator.flatMap(sub))`, then `nodes -- sub(prefix)`. Even better, keep each node's regions on the node, so regionOwner is cleaned locally too.

smells.smell: The same subtree is measured again at every level. measureItem measures a whole subtree, then place, layoutChildren and measuredKids measure the kids again, so the work is O(n·depth). tableSize runs once in measureElement and once more in layoutChildren. When a container's natural size changes, relayout (834-836) also throws away the work it did at its own level.
smells.fix: Keep the result of the measure in Measured (the kids' Measured, the table cols) and reuse it in place, or memoize per Loc inside one layout pass. Check the natural-size change before re-arranging the kids.

smells.smell: textWidth(last) is computed again for every word or glyph, and `acc.init :+` rebuilds the accumulator. The cost is O(words × width) for each text node. It is paid in measure and again in paint (Paint.scala:300 wraps the same text again).
smells.fix: It stays pure. Fold over `(lines, cur, curW)` and carry the current width. Store the wrapped lines in Kind.Txt so that paint does not wrap again.

smells.smell: `String.replaceAll("<[^>]*>", "")` compiles a regex for every RawHtml in every flatten pass.
smells.fix: `private val Tag = java.util.regex.Pattern.compile("<[^>]*>")`, then `Tag.matcher(v).replaceAll("")`.

smells.smell: Stringly-typed tree paths. A child index is `i.toString`, region content is "~", and a foreach item is s"#$key". The alias is transparent, so any Vector[String] is a Loc. Each Map lookup also hashes the whole path, which costs O(depth) (clipOf and relayout do many lookups).
smells.fix: `opaque type Loc = Vector[Step]` with `enum Step { case Child(i: Int); case Content; case Item(key: String) }`, plus a cached hash if a profile asks for it.

smells.smell: An Any-typed bound value. Paint recovers its type at runtime with `.toString`, `.contains(true)` and `collect { case d: Double }`. Runner also casts c.value with asInstanceOf.
smells.fix: Use a typed enum `BoundValue { Str(s); Bool(b); Num(d) }` that is set where the SignalRef is read.

smells.where: Paint.scala:458-497 vs Layout.scala:201-207; Paint.scala:580-587 vs Props.scala:254-261
smells.smell: Duplicated logic. Select options are taken out twice (Layout for the width, Paint for the label) and the `(label + " " * r.w).take(...) + "▾"` line is repeated. The list marker text ("• " and s"${i + 1}. ") is built in Paint, and its width again in Props.
smells.fix: One `Picker.options(el): Vector[(value, label)]` and one `ListMarker.text(style, index)`. Layout, Props and Paint all use them.

smells.smell: A magic 'infinity' sentinel, `Rect(0, 0, Int.MaxValue / 2, Int.MaxValue / 2)`.
smells.fix: Start from the screen node's rect, `laid.nodes.get(Loc.screen).fold(Rect.empty)(_.rect)`. The walk already reaches that node, so the result is the same.

smells.smell: `text.drop(skip)` drops UTF-16 chars where it means cells. A left clip would split a surrogate pair or shift wide characters. Margins are clamped to 0 or more (Props.scala:168), so a node never starts left of its clip today. This is latent.
smells.fix: Skip by cells with TextEdit.graphemes and textWidth. Or put the clip rect in the Op and let the kernel skip graphemes.

smells.smell: A misleading claim and the wrong module. The Scaladoc says Canvas is 'THE ONE MUTABLE PLACE', but TextEdit also has var and while. Canvas, the foreign boundary, lives in the same file as the painter, which can be pure.
smells.fix: Move Canvas to its own Canvas.scala boundary file (see the sites). After the TextEdit replacements, the claim is true.

smells.smell: A case class with 11 positional fields, built positionally in 3 places with literals like `Vector.empty, None, 0`. Kind.Txt(text, wrap: Boolean) and TextEdit.key(..., readOnly: Boolean) are mild boolean blindness, and TextEdit returns `(String, Int)` tuples.
smells.fix: Use named arguments with defaults for Node. A `Field(text, caret)` case class for TextEdit's in and out. A `Wrap` enum is optional.

audits.sliceVerdict: Layout is already pure and contains no var, while, null or try. Its real problems are types (4 casts, Any-typed bound values, stringly paths), duplication (the table-row logic has drifted, and this probably makes a foreach inside a tbody never update) and two per-frame perf traps (Laid.without filters the whole map, subtrees are measured repeatedly). Geometry is pure apart from dead members, and TextEdit is pure at its API, with 3 small var/while sites off the hot path that are cheap to replace. The impurity that matters is in Paint.scala. A painter that could be pure writes cells straight into Canvas as it goes. Canvas reports a failure by throwing a TuiError that Tui.scala turns back into an error, keeps a hidden writes counter, and carries a test busy-spin in production code. The real hot loops (clear, fillBg, the flush diff and setStringn) all mutate the foreign jatatui Buffer, so they are legitimate KEEP-EDGE kernels. The change that gives most value is to split Paint into a pure `Paint.plan(laid, env, damage): FramePlan` (a Chunk of Ops) plus one `Canvas.draw(plan): FrameOut < (Sync & Abort[TuiError])` seam in its own Canvas.scala. That removes the writes counter, the throw-for-control-flow and the direct mutation, and it keeps the per-cell loops in one documented kernel.

sites.construct: Thread shutdown hook 'tui4s-stop', java.util.concurrent.CountDownLatch, fiber.unsafe.onComplete, Sync.Unsafe.defer, import AllowUnsafe.embrace.danger (154), blocking restored.await(2 s) on the hook thread
sites.what: block starts the run on a fiber and registers a JVM hook. The hook interrupts the fiber, then waits up to 2 s on a latch. Two things count the latch down: the release, through the restored callback that goes through Tui.runWith and TerminalIO, and the end of the fiber. In the same TuiApp run, TerminalIO.opened also registers a second hook, 'tui4s-restore', which calls release() directly on the hook thread. TuiAppTest waits for hooks.added.size == 2.
sites.why: SIGTERM, SIGINT and System.exit must restore the terminal. Hooks run on JVM threads, not on fibers. The direct release is for a fiber that is stuck in System.exit and never sees the interrupt.
sites.risk: Terminal restore under SIGTERM and System.exit, concurrency of hooks and release, exit codes 130 and 143. Session.close is idempotent and synchronized (Session.scala:89), so a double release is safe. This is concurrency and terminal-restore code, so it needs the adversarial check, the three TuiAppTest hook tests and the PTY kit.

sites.construct: hooks.shuttingDown called twice. Each call adds and removes a real JVM probe hook and uses IllegalStateException for control flow.
sites.what: Tells a JVM stop apart from a quit, so that runMain skips onExit and returns 1.
sites.why: The restore hook can end the run as a quit, so the outcome of the run cannot tell a stop from a quit.
sites.risk: Exit code and onExit skip on a JVM stop. A stop that runs none of our hooks (after the run ended) is no longer seen, but then the terminal is already restored.

```scala
private final case class Fwd(stream: PrintStream, bytes: Forward)
private final case class State(out: Maybe[Fwd], err: Maybe[Fwd], realOut: Maybe[PrintStream], realErr: Maybe[PrintStream], all: Chunk[Fwd], pinned: Boolean, active: Maybe[LogSink])
private var state = State.empty // the only var; read and written under OutputCapture.synchronized
```

sites.construct: mutable.ArrayDeque ring plus 5 vars (4 nullable: out, finished, problem, lateFile) under synchronized
sites.what: An implicit state machine: open to a file or to a memory ring, then finished (late lines go to the file or, if important, to stderr at once). A file write failure falls back to the ring.
sites.why: line() is called from forwarder threads and from Kyo's log daemon fiber. finish() is called from the release, which can run on a JVM hook thread.
sites.replacement:
Keep the lock. Make the state one value:
```scala
private enum State:
  case ToFile(w: java.io.Writer, path: Path)
  case ToRing(kept: scala.collection.immutable.Queue[String], dropped: Long, problem: Maybe[String])
  case Done(err: PrintStream, late: Maybe[Path])
private var state: State // the only var, under `synchronized`
def line(text: String, keep: Keep): Unit = synchronized { state = LogSink.step(state, text, keep, capacity) }
```
The ring math is a pure function on ToRing (enqueue, then drop the head and add 1 to dropped above capacity). Only ToFile and Done do IO. Combinations that cannot happen today (out != null and finished != null) can then not be written at all.

```scala
object LogSink:
  def open(file: Option[Path], capacity: Int = 200)(using Frame): LogSink < Sync = Sync.defer(file match
    case None    => new LogSink(State.ToRing(Queue.empty, 0, Absent), capacity, file)
    case Some(p) => Result(Files.newBufferedWriter(p, UTF_8, CREATE, APPEND)).foldError(
      w => new LogSink(State.ToFile(w, p), capacity, file),
      e => new LogSink(State.ToRing(Queue.empty, 0, Present(s"tui4s: the log file $p cannot be written: ${e.exception}")), capacity, file)))
// Tui.runWith: Sync.acquireReleaseWith(LogSink.open(options.logFile))(s => Sync.defer(s.finish(err())))(sink => ...)
```

Also (plausible, not tested): the check `ne out && ne originalOut` does not see an older forwarder. A program that restores a saved older forwarder therefore gets a forwarder of a forwarder, and realErr then returns a forwarder.

smells.fix: Use Clock.live.unsafe and state the skew (milliseconds) in the Scaladoc. Upstream: ask Kyo for a public Event, or a timestamp parameter on Log.Unsafe.

audits.sliceVerdict: This slice is in better shape than the rest of the app. Most of its impure code is a real JVM boundary: the System.out/err forwarders, PrintStream, the shutdown hooks, System.exit and the Log.Unsafe backend. That code is locked with care. The public files (Tui, TuiOptions, TuiError, FrameStats, package) are already Kyo pipelines or plain data, and their public shapes need no change; only TuiError's `cause: Throwable | Null` can be tightened, with the same erasure. The real problem is the shape of the code, not its purity: 8 nullable vars in a global object and 6 in LogSink instead of one immutable state value each, null sentinels (Capture(null), t = null, inputFailure), a per-byte while loop on a ByteArrayOutputStream that is a pure fold in disguise, and a sink that is finished at three places. The change with the most value is one JVM-stop boundary: a single hook that marks the stop, interrupts the run fiber, falls back to the synchronous release and waits for restored, installed by Tui.runWith for both entry points. It removes the second hook, the exception-driven shuttingDown probe, the restored callback that goes through runWith and TerminalIO, and most of TuiApp.block. It is terminal-restore and concurrency code, so even in lean mode it needs the adversarial check and the PTY run.

audits.slice: testkit-examples. Rubric: the provisional rubric, plus the user's functional-design and scala-functional-design skills, which loaded during this run. Read-only; no sbt.

sites.construct: A sentinel value compared with `eq` (`endMark`, a fake FrameStats with seq = Long.MinValue), put back into the channel after each take; `Abort.run[Closed](...).map(_.getOrThrow)` on channels that are never closed; firstFrame polls `frames.poll` and sleeps 5 ms
sites.what: Signals 'the run has ended' to the methods that wait for a frame (send, nextFrame, drainFrames, firstFrame). Each method finds the mark by reference, offers it back, then panics.
sites.why: Review R1-8/R2-7: after the run ends, a wait must fail and not hang. The channels are `initUnscoped` and never closed, so a mark was added by hand. The `Abort[Closed]` handling can never fire: it only erases the effect from the type, and `getOrThrow` would rethrow inside `map`.
sites.risk: Concurrency: this is the end-of-run contract (OS-34, R1-8, R2-7). 'The key that ended the run still gets its frame' still holds, because closeAwaitEmpty keeps the buffered frames takeable. Closing the inbox also fixes a latent hang: today, `inbox.put` on a full inbox after the run ended never returns. No public API change. Run the existing Headless end-of-run tests.

sites.construct: `Sync.defer(java.lang.System.nanoTime())` twice and a sleep-poll loop (`Clock.let(Clock.live)(Async.sleep(5.millis))`)
sites.what: Wall-clock polling every 5 ms, for awaitEnd (run.done) and awaitScreen (a full Screen snapshot each time).
sites.why: OS-34: never join the run fiber from an interruptible wait. The live clock is used because a test can run under Clock.withTimeControl.
sites.risk: Concurrency (OS-34). Ending the wait on a Promise is not a join of `run`, so the deadlock argument still holds. Test timing: keep the live clock.

sites.what: Reads the mutable TestBackend under the monitor that Canvas holds while it flushes or resizes (Paint.scala:51, 70, 166), so a screen is never a torn frame.

Add `Canvas.read[A](f: Backend => A): A < Sync` (Sync.defer + synchronized in Paint.scala) and call `canvas.read(Screen.of)` here. Also, `lines` calls `buf.cellAt(x, y)` with no `area.x/area.y` offset, while Screen.of adds them: harmless on a TestBackend (origin 0), but the two snapshot paths disagree.

sites.construct: `java.util.Optional` `isPresent` then `c.get`; reflection `getClass.getSimpleName.replaceAll("([a-z])([A-Z])", ...)` for each coloured cell
sites.what: Converts a jatatui colour to the testkit's colour string.
sites.why: jatatui Color is a Java sealed interface of records (Reset, Black, ... LightBlue, Rgb, Indexed). The class name was used to avoid writing 16 cases.
sites.replacement:
import scala.jdk.OptionConverters.*
def colour(c: java.util.Optional[JColor]): Option[String] = c.toScala.filter(_ != JColor.RESET).map(name)
private def name(c: JColor): String = c match
  case rgb: JColor.Rgb     => f"#${rgb.r}%02x${rgb.g}%02x${rgb.b}%02x"
  case idx: JColor.Indexed => s"indexed:${idx.i}"
  case _: JColor.Black     => "black"
  case _: JColor.LightBlue => "light-blue"
  // ... one case for each of the 16 named records

sites.construct: `Abort.catching[IOException] { Files.exists(...); Files.readAllLines(...).toArray.map(_.toString) }` and `Abort.catching(Files.writeString(...))` with no Sync.defer
sites.what: Reads and writes the todo file.
sites.why: The author assumed Abort.catching suspends. In Kyo RC7 it does not: ArrowEffect.handleCont (kyo-kernel ArrowEffect.scala:131-132) evaluates the block at once (`val v0 = v`) inside a try. The file is therefore read when `Todo.app(file)` is evaluated, not when the effect runs, and the `< Sync` in the signature is only widening. Running the same program value twice reuses the first read.
sites.risk: None in behavior today. TuiApp and Headless happen to call `ui` on the run fiber, so the timing is the same. Users copy this file, so the wrong idiom spreads.

sites.where: examples/src/main/scala/examples/todo/Todo.scala:139-211 (app; nextId AtomicInt 148; delete 171-173; move 174-179; listKeys 180-194; saveAll 195-201)
sites.construct: A 70-line for-comprehension: four loose SignalRefs and a separate AtomicInt, eight effect closures, two-step writes across refs, and an `(... ): Any < Async` ascription that guards against the 'lift trap'
sites.what: All the state and actions of the Todo app. `delete` writes `items`, then `cursor`. `move` reads `items`, then writes `cursor`. `add` makes four separate steps.
sites.why: Prototype style. It ignores the rules of examples/README.md ('An ordinary class can group signals, derived values, and actions') and experiments/ui-state/README.md ('Pure Var transitions applied inside an atomic SignalRef update'; eager app-scoped groups).
sites.replacement:
final case class Model(items: Chunk[Item], cursor: Int, nextId: Int) derives CanEqual:
  def add(text: String): Model = if text.isBlank then this else copy(items = items :+ Item(nextId, text.trim, false), nextId = nextId + 1)
  def toggle: Model = at(i => Chunk(i.copy(done = !i.done)))
  def delete: Model = at(_ => Chunk.empty).clampCursor
  def move(d: Int): Model = copy(cursor = cursor + d).clampCursor
  def rows: Chunk[Row] = items.zipWithIndex.map((t, i) => Row(t, i == cursor))
  private def clampCursor = copy(cursor = cursor.max(0).min((items.size - 1).max(0)))
  private def at(f: Item => Chunk[Item]) =
    if items.isDefinedAt(cursor) then copy(items = items.take(cursor) ++ f(items(cursor)) ++ items.drop(cursor + 1)) else this

final class TodoStore(file: String, model: SignalRef[Model], val draft: SignalRef[String], val status: SignalRef[String]):
  val rows: Signal[Chunk[Row]] = model.map(_.rows)
  val count: Signal[String]    = model.map(m => s"${m.items.count(!_.done)} open / ${m.items.size}")
  def update(f: Model => Model): Unit < Sync = model.updateAndGet(f).unit   // one atomic, pure transition
  val add: Unit < Sync = draft.get.map(t => if t.isBlank then Kyo.unit else update(_.add(t)).andThen(draft.set("")))
  val save: Unit < Sync = model.get.map(m => Abort.run[IOException](Todo.save(file, m.items)).map {
    case Result.Success(_) => status.set(s"saved ${m.items.size} items to $file")
    case Result.Failure(e) => status.set(s"save failed: ${e.getMessage}")
    case Result.Panic(e)   => status.set(s"save failed: $e") })
  val listKeys: KeyboardEvent => Unit < Sync = _.key match
    case Keyboard.ArrowUp | Keyboard.Char('k')   => update(_.move(-1))
    case Keyboard.ArrowDown | Keyboard.Char('j') => update(_.move(1))
    case Keyboard.Space                          => update(_.toggle)
    case Keyboard.Char('d')                      => update(_.delete)
    case _                                       => Kyo.unit
// app = TodoStore.init(file).map(view); the AtomicInt, atCursor and the lift-trap comment go away; Model is tested without a UI
sites.risk: Low. Behavior stays the same; TodoSuite and the PTY `todo` row cover it. One visible improvement: delete becomes one atomic change, so no frame shows a cursor past the end.

sites.why: Component.initial is pure in the core API, and core's Component.ui (Component.scala:82-89) calls it under `AllowUnsafe.embrace.danger` each time `.ui` is evaluated. So the example hid a global side effect in `initial`.

audits.sliceVerdict: This slice is in better shape than the rest of the app: the examples have almost no raw `while` or `var`, and Dashboard, Widgets and the counters already use the target style (scoped Fiber.init, Loop, Stream and Emit, Signal-derived views). The worst impurity is in two examples users copy. Todo.load and Todo.save rely on Abort.catching, which does not suspend in Kyo RC7, so the file IO is not deferred. TabsView hides a JVM-global AtomicLong inside a pure-looking `initial`. In the testkit, Headless rebuilds by hand, with a reference-compared sentinel, two 5 ms sleep-poll loops, and `Abort[Closed]` handling that can never fire, what a half-closed Kyo Channel and a Promise give natively. Screen.scala has four hand-written loops and private copies of TextEdit.graphemes and Layout.textWidth. The one change with the most value is to rewrite Todo as an app-scoped TodoStore over a pure Model updated with `SignalRef.updateAndGet`, with `Sync.defer` around the file IO: it is the template users copy, and today it breaks the state rules of the repo's own READMEs. The second is to close the Headless frame channel when the run ends, which deletes about 60 lines of sentinel and polling code and keeps the end-of-run contract.

plan.verdict: The app is not "whiles everywhere". The five audits found 93 impure sites. There are about a dozen real while loops, and all of them are in edge files, TextEdit or Screen. The reactive tree and Layout are already immutable values threaded through Kyo Loop, folds and recursion. The user's verdict still holds for the shape of the code. The edge code is written like Java: 9 volatile or nullable fields in Session, TerminalIO and Crossterm, 14 more in OutputCapture and LogSink, four hand-written copies of "run every step, keep the first error" with three different catch policies, and exceptions for expected outcomes. Runner and Mount use java.util.concurrent atomics and a weak synchronized set where Kyo AtomicRef, Fiber.use and a pure World field do the same job. Paint looks pure but mutates the jatatui buffer while it decides what to draw. The examples that users copy teach wrong idioms: Abort.catching does not suspend in RC7, and TabsView hides global state. The plan keeps 29 sites as real boundaries in one package, tui4s.internal.edge. It keeps 3 justified kernel functions, replaces about 50 sites with Kyo or plain functional forms, and deletes 13. Phases P1 to P4 give most of the value for about half of the diff. P5, the pure painter, is the largest single change. P6, a single JVM stop hook, is the riskiest step and can be skipped. I spot-checked 10 audit claims in the code and in the Kyo RC7 sources, and all of them held. One premise did not hold: kyo-test RC7 has no property-test API (the jar has no PropertyTest or Gen), so the property tests need a decision.

principles: P1 No impure syntax outside the edge. Main code (core and examples) has no var, while/do, null literal, `| Null` type, return, throw, asInstanceOf/isInstanceOf, synchronized, @volatile, java.util.concurrent, Thread, System.*, Runtime.*, AllowUnsafe, Sync.Unsafe or .unsafe, except in tui4s.internal.edge and in the allowlisted lines below. Check: scalafixAll --check with DisableSyntax, plus scripts/purity-check.sh.

P2 Every KEEP-KERNEL function is marked. It carries a `// KERNEL:` marker that names the hot path and a measured number (for example cells per frame and renderNanos). Its mutation is local and nothing escapes. A pure reference test or property compares it with a spec. Check: purity-check fails on a kernel suppression without a KERNEL reason. The list holds exactly Canvas.write, Canvas.diff and LineSplit.feed.

P3 One seam for each foreign operation. An edge API returns `A < Sync` or `A < (Sync & Abort[TuiError])`. The only synchronous exceptions are the release that a JVM hook must run (Session.close, JvmStop), and its Scaladoc names the restore guarantees G1-G11 that it keeps. Check: no AllowUnsafe parameter in a signature outside edge/.
P4 Null stops at the Java line. A Scala-owned type is never nullable. A Java result that can be null becomes Maybe(javaCall()) on the line of the call. Check: regex `\|\s*Null` outside edge/ is 0.

P5 Errors are values. Expected failures are Abort[TuiError] or Result. A throw is allowed only to rethrow a VirtualMachineError and for the framework AssertionError in Screen.assertScreen. A Panic is never mapped to a clean quit or swallowed by `case _` after Abort.run. Check: noThrows plus review, and a grep for `case _\s*=>` right after Abort.run.

P6 Shared state is allocated in an effect. Concurrent state is a Kyo AtomicRef, AtomicBoolean, Channel, Promise or SignalRef that an `X.init: X < Sync` creates, never a constructor body or an object field. The only exceptions are the three allowlisted JVM globals: the OutputCapture state, the ComponentSpec weak registry and the JvmStop flag. Check: lint plus a review of each `new` in a class body.

P7 Every fiber has an owner and a stop path. It runs under Fiber.use or Fiber.init, or Mount.fork puts it in the gauge (removed on completion). Fiber.initUnscoped appears only in Mount.fork. Check: grep for initUnscoped finds exactly 1 site, and liveFibers == 0 after every run in the tests.

P8 A fiber's failure is visible. A failure or a non-interrupt Panic of a background fiber goes to Log.error (the file sink, never stdout) or into a typed result. Check: a test where a failing useEffect writes one ERROR line.
P9 Time comes from Kyo Clock. Outside edge/, use Clock.nowMonotonic and Clock.deadline, not System.nanoTime, so that tests can control time. Check: the System.* regex.

P10 Effects are no wider than used. A function that only allocates or reads is `< Sync`, not `< Async`, and Sync.defer is used where Sync.Unsafe.defer is not needed. Check: review item. For a public signature, run versionPolicyCheck.
P11 Domain meaning is typed. New or changed code uses enums or records, not Boolean flags, string tags or positional tuples (SessionStep, Click, Keep, Mode, Entered, LogLine). Check: review item.

P12 A function that becomes pure gets a property test against a spec or an oracle: TextEdit, LineSplit, Paint.plan (with the old painter as the oracle), the Todo Model and the LogSink ring. Check: each phase's exit lists its properties.

P13 The restore contract is executable. The step order and the guarantees G1-G11 stay in the Session Scaladoc. Each one has a SessionTest or TerminalIOTest assertion or a PTY row. Any change under edge/ runs the PTY kit once (53 rows, 68 screen checks, kill -TERM 143, kill -INT 130).

notWorthIt: Session.close as one synchronous release under a JVM monitor, with a bounded Thread.join. A JVM shutdown hook has no fiber. Scope finalizers run on Async and would need the Kyo scheduler during the shutdown, and Fiber.init awaits its fibers. Clean up only the inside (P3).

The input thread as a platform daemon thread. The native crossterm read() cannot be interrupted. A daemon thread whose poll hangs does not keep the JVM alive. A JNI poll on a Kyo worker would count as load in SchedulerProbe, so every settle would run until its max of 100 ms per frame.

The message form Msg.InputFailed for an input failure. It drops a failure that comes after a Msg.Quit, but today that case fails with TerminalIO. An AtomicRef.Unsafe[Maybe[Throwable]] keeps the behavior for less cost.

The ComponentSpec weak identity registry. The kyo-ui AST and kyo.Signal are sealed, so there is no other side channel. Making node() effectful would change the public return types (Hooks.component: UI and the conversion to HtmlChildVal).

The Component state cast. Component#State is path-dependent, and a full fix needs a `given Tag[State]` on the public Component. Keep one cast in one helper. Optionally add the class to the key so that two classes cannot share one state.

SchedulerDefaults.applyIfUnset and the TuiApp constructor's side effects. They must run before the first Kyo class initializes and before scala.Console binds its stream, so no Kyo effect can wrap them.

The `arguments` var and System.exit in TuiApp. `args` is a pure public accessor, written once before the run fiber starts (KyoApp does the same). A Local or Env would make it effectful. System.exit is the end of the process, and Runtime.halt would skip the restore.
